defects.section: 6 (shifts.py: format_shift is the inverse of parse_shift)
defects.repro: format_shift(Interval(0, 1440)) returns '00:00-00:00'. Interval(0, 1440) is valid under section 6. parse_shift('00:00-00:00') raises ValueError because start equals end. So format_shift emits text that parse_shift rejects. Interval(0, 2880) has the same problem.
defects.fix: Decide on the contract. Either restrict Interval length to under 1440, or have format_shift reject intervals of 1440 or more. Alternatively, document that those intervals are not formattable.
defects.if_skipped: A full-day or 48-hour interval gets formatted into text that cannot be parsed back. This only affects callers that build such intervals directly.

gaps: Overnight shifts spilling into the next day are not seen by Schedule.assign conflicts or coverage_gaps. Section 6 only says 'same day', so I treated this as designed and did not test it.
Non-str or non-date arguments are not specified, so I did not test them.

advisory.problem: AC-006 checks only three invalid inputs. A lazy parser that only checks for a '-' and a valid hour range, or one that accepts '9:00-17:30' or equal start and end times, would still pass. The brief's other ValueError cases are untested.
advisory.evidence: A parser that rejects only empty text, text without ':' and hours above 23 passes all three cases. The brief's AC lists only these three inputs, so this is not blocking.
